div.div: Morphology from node-level measurements. Can a cell-level phenotype (CalMorph) be predicted from the genotype, and does the strain's own measured gene-level modality (expression, proteome) help when given as input? Panels a and b describe the data; c is the inductive arm; d, e and f need the strain's measurement (transductive); g is more training data for the measured modalities, not a panel of its own.

div.div:
The strain sets
three single-deletion panels and their overlaps: morphology 4,695, expression 1,554, proteome 4,476; morph. and expr. 1,439, morph. and prot. 4,281, all three 1,321. Counts, no statistic.

The conditioning triangle
the same contrast on the other two sides: proteome given the strain's expression +0.054 (11 of 11), expression given its proteome +0.033 (10 of 11), both below their ridge; morphology is the third vertex.

div.div:
More training strains for the measured modalities: the 1,011 natural isolates (Peter 2018)
Not a morphology panel: no CalMorph exists for these strains. The idea is to add them as extra training data for the expression head (Caudal 2024 pan-transcriptome, built, 943 isolates) and the proteome head (Muenzner 2024, 796 isolates, next build), about 1,000 strains whose expression differs far more between strains than the deletion panels do, and then ask whether the deletion-strain heads, and through them the transductive morphology arms in d, improve. Open question first: how an isolate's genotype enters a model that takes a set of deleted genes. Idea only; likely not in time for this round.
